explanation: I grepped all of Mathlib for `IsCompactElement` and read every hit: Mathlib/Order/CompactlyGenerated/Basic.lean (definition, `isCompactElement_iff_le_of_directed_sSup_le`, `isCompactElement_iff_exists_le_sSup_of_le_sSup`, `isCompactElement_iff_exists_le_iSup_of_le_iSup`, `IsCompactElement.exists_finset_of_le_iSup`, `directed_sSup_lt_of_lt`, `isCompactElement_finsetSup`, `IsCompactElement.iSup`, `IsCompactElement.sSup`, atom/coatomic results), Mathlib/Order/CompactlyGenerated/Intervals.lean (`isCompactElement` for `Iic a`), plus the occurrences in Topology/Sets/Opens, LinearAlgebra/Span, RingTheory/Ideal/Span, RingTheory/Finiteness, FieldTheory/IntermediateField/Adjoin, Order/BooleanGenerators, Algebra/Lie/Submodule. None of them mentions an order isomorphism (`≃o`), an order embedding or a Galois connection; grepping `Mathlib` for combinations of `IsCompactElement` with `≃o`, `map`/`image`, or for `compact` inside the `OrderIso` files returns nothing. Mathlib only supplies the ingredients used in the proof (`OrderIso.isLUB_image'`, `DirectedOn.mono_comp`, `OrderIso.le_symm_apply`), so a `special_case` derivation would require the whole pull-back/push-forward argument of substance, not one or two lines. Hence no Mathlib duplicate was found.
